story: Gary is at his workbench at home, finalizing wiring sketches for tomorrow's walk to the committee, with every piece marked strap-on and removable. Across town, Donna is running third-shot drop drills against the wall at Rec Center pickleball court 1, getting ready to coach Gary when he arrives. Out on Magnolia Loop, Hal is counting flamingos in Donna's flock from the street and jotting the tally in his notebook, while Rosa, content, has just thanked him for coming and headed in to put her feet up.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Finalize and label the wiring sketches, marking everything strap-on and removable, ready for tomorrow's walk to the committee
Donna (pickleball court 1): Run third-shot drop drills against the wall so I can coach Gary when he arrives
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos from the street and log the tally in my notebook

gary.thought_process: I'm home, nobody around, and the tomorrow-at-nine walk with Rosa and Hal to the committee is set. My Review application is filed, so nothing gets bolted on until the stamp, but nothing stops me from tidying the sketches. Gary's workbench is right here. I'll clean up the wiring sketches, label the strap-on mounts and make sure every drawing says removable, so Hal finds nothing to object to and Rosa's trust is earned. Useful work, and it keeps the evening from feeling empty.

parameters.content: Finalize and label the wiring sketches, marking everything strap-on and removable, ready for tomorrow's walk to the committee

donna.thought_process: It's 7:17 PM and I've already studied the ladder board, checked the kiosk (two hours max, set for Gary), and warmed up with solo serves and dinks. Gary isn't in sight yet. No point repeating myself or pestering anyone. Best use of this hour is actually getting reps in on the court so I'm sharp when Gary shows up, since he's never played and I'll be carrying him in the ladder match. Keep it simple and stay within the two-hour reservation.

parameters.content: Run third-shot drop drills against the wall so I can coach Gary when he arrives

hal.thought_process: Rosa's right here on the Loop and already offered to walk the sketches over at nine tomorrow. I accepted last tick, so asking again would be nagging. The flamingo count still needs checking, though, and the flock is the one thing on this street I haven't tallied today. L-02 says three ornaments maximum visible from the street, and I want the number in my notebook before the committee meeting. Do the job, then go home to the notebook and the cornbread.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos from the street and log the tally in my notebook

rosa.thought_process: Hal just confirmed nine sharp tomorrow, and Gary's headed home to finish his sketches, so the plan is settled. No need to re-invite anyone. It's 7:17 PM, the dinner went well, and I've been overcommitted all day. The best next step is to wrap this up warmly and go home to rest, rather than repeat myself. Hal's been prickly, so a short, friendly send-off keeps goodwill going.

parameters.content: Nine sharp it is, Hal. Thanks for coming tonight and for hearing us out. I'm heading in to put my feet up, I've earned it.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
